attributes.body_ja:
「何（なに）しろ」は、代名詞（だいめいし）「何（なに）」と「する」の命令形（めいれいけい）「しろ」の組（く）み合（あ）わせですが、一（ひと）つの副詞（ふくし）として扱（あつか）われることが多（おお）いです。この表現（ひょうげん）は、どのような状況（じょうきょう）でも、結局（けっきょく） (A) という結論（けつろん）になることを表（あらわ）します。

「何（なに）しろ」は文（ぶん）の頭（あたま）か、文中（ぶんちゅう）の二（ふた）つ目（め）の節（せつ）の頭（あたま）で主（おも）に使（つか）われます。

「何（なに）しろ」は、(A) の理由（りゆう）や説明（せつめい）を強調（きょうちょう）するために、「から」や「ので」のような言葉（ことば）を含（ふく）む文（ぶん）と一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）われることもよくあります。
attributes.body:
Although a combination of the substitute noun 何（なに） and the imperative form of する, しろ, 何（なに）しろ is often considered to be a singular adverb that carries the meaning of 'no wonder', or 'after all'. A more literal translation would be something like 'whatever the case, (A)', and just expresses that in any circumstance, only one conclusion can accurately be drawn in regard to (A).

何（なに）しろ will frequently appear at the beginning of a sentence, or at the start of the second clause.

何（なに）しろ will regularly be seen partnered with statements including words like から or ので, in order to emphasize an explanation or reason as to why (A) is the way it is.

何しろ introduces a reason or emphasis, often justifying a statement, as in 何しろ忙しいので行けません (In any case, I can’t go because I’m busy). どうせ conveys resignation or futility, as in どうせ無理だ (It’s hopeless anyway). Both can be translated as ‘in any case’, but 何しろ is explanatory, while どうせ carries a negative, defeatist tone.

attributes.body: にしても～にしても structures a conditional to show indifference between possibilities, as in 雨にしても雪にしても中止だ (Whether rain or snow, it’s canceled). 何しろ introduces a reason or explanation, often with resignation, as in 忙しい、何しろ締め切りが近い (I’m busy; after all, the deadline is near).

attributes.body: Both can mean after all, but differ in nuance. 何といっても emphasizes the decisive point, as in 何といっても経験が大事だ (Above all, experience matters). 何しろ introduces a reason or background explanation, as in 忙しいんです。何しろ締め切りが近い (I’m busy, after all the deadline is near).

attributes.body: Both include しろ but are unrelated in usage. にせよ・にしろ means even if (A), as in 結果が悪いにせよ挑戦するべきだ (Even if the result is bad, you should try). 何しろ appears at the start of a sentence meaning anyway or after all, as in 何しろ忙しいので行けません (Anyway, I can’t go because I’m busy).

attributes.body: 何しろ and にしても are similar in that both have a general sense of 'no matter' or 'regardless', they are used quite differently. 何しろ comes at the beginning of a sentence to express 'after all, (A)', while にしても follows a noun or phrase to specifically state 'even if (A), still (B)'.
